key_insight: A hybrid LLM-guided search loop is the most consistent way to discover strong quantum reservoir computing architectures, but only when paired with classical optimization safeguards.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum machine learning, the work shows that architecture search—not just the quantum model itself—can materially improve performance under tight evaluation budgets.
method: Formulate QRC design as constrained black-box architecture search.
Compare random, evolutionary, Bayesian/TPE, LLM-agent, and hybrid LLM+memory/mutation/crossover policies.
Evaluate on NARMA10, Mackey-Glass forecasting, and temporal parity with fixed simulator budgets.
evidence_signal: Across three seeds and a 25-evaluation budget, the hybrid method ranked first on NARMA10 and temporal parity, second on Mackey-Glass, and reduced Mackey-Glass error by 23.6% vs. random search.
watch_item: The results do not imply that LLMs are universal optimizers; performance depends on careful hybridization, validation, and reproducible search controls.
paper_title: Hybrid LLM-Guided Search for Quantum Reservoir Architecture Design
